brief.userPrompt: Tuesday, 13 October 2026, a mild autumn morning at Halvorsen State University in Marlow Falls, Iowa. The exercise starts at 09:15. At 09:02 graduate student Lena Park in Dr. Anika Rao's bacterial genetics laboratory (Lindgren third floor, shared centrifuge room with Dr. Tomas Eklund's cell biology laboratory) hears a tube crack in a rotor and may have had a splash to the face and a small cut to her glove hand; the material is a Risk Group 2 culture covered by the laboratory's approved protocol (never describe technique or the organism beyond that). Dr. Rao calls the BSO Marcus Tran at 09:20 (the PI's target is within 2 hours; the form is due within 24 hours). Pressure points the exercise must cover: the BSO orders stop-work in the centrifuge room (target within 30 minutes of the report) and sends Lena for medical evaluation (target within 60 minutes), but the approved protocol says no post-exposure prophylaxis is needed while Occupational Health physician Dr. Mbeki wants to evaluate; the Occupational Health Clinic is open until 17:00 and the after-hours route is Marlow Falls Regional Medical Center; a program officer at a federal sponsor says informally that it does not need NIH reporting, while the Iowa Corn Growers Board award (fictional, domain cornboard.example) requires notice in 72 hours, shorter than the HSU 7-day target; the IBC chair Prof. Dennis Okafor must classify the event (reportable to NIH through the IBC, internal incident, records discrepancy) and record the basis, with the IBC report to the NIH Office of Science Policy due in 30 days and the chair erring toward reporting if uncertain; the clock board kept by Joel Whitcomb shows PI to BSO in 24 hours, BSO to IBC chair in 3 days, sponsor in 7 days; a second laboratory discovers a freezer inventory mismatch the same morning, which is a records discrepancy and not an incident, and someone raises select agents although HSU holds none, so the team must classify it and not file a select agent report; at 11:30 a student in the campus forum claims a lab leak and the student newspaper calls, while University Communications (Renata Delgado) holds a statement that names no worker, laboratory or organism. The SimCell plays the worker's advisor and lab mates, a sponsor program officer, NIH OSP, the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services, Marlow Falls Fire Department, the Occupational Health Clinic physician Dr. Mbeki and reporters. The BSO advisor explains deadlines and never gives agent handling detail.
constraints: Every email address of the university uses the exercise domain hsu.example; sponsors and outside parties use fictional domains such as cornboard.example; never a real institution, company or newspaper domain.
No agent technique, culture method or handling detail appears anywhere; the organism is only a Risk Group 2 culture under an approved protocol, and the worker is never named in public statements.
Notification clocks are the plan's: PI to biosafety officer 24 hours, IBC chair 3 days, sponsor 7 days (or the award term), NIH 30 days; HSU holds no select agents.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; NIH OSP, the sponsor, public health, the fire department, the clinic physician, the student worker's lab mates, reporters and the public are played by the SimCell.

overview.theme: The worker's health before the protocol, which deadline actually governs, deciding and recording what kind of event it is, and answering a "lab leak" claim without naming anyone.
overview.threat: At 09:02 on Tuesday, 13 October 2026, before STARTEX, a tube cracked inside a centrifuge rotor in the shared centrifuge room on the third floor of the Lindgren Life Sciences Building. Graduate student Lena Park of the bacterial genetics laboratory may have had a splash to the face and a small cut to her gloved hand. The material is a Risk Group 2 culture covered by the laboratory's approved protocol. There was no attacker: the cause was an equipment failure. The failure stops work in a room that the bacterial genetics laboratory shares with a cell biology laboratory, and it starts the PI-to-BSO, IBC chair, sponsor and NIH notification clocks. That same morning a second laboratory finds a freezer inventory mismatch, and someone in the room raises select agents, even though HSU holds none.
overview.operationalImpact: The PI calls the Biosafety Officer at 09:20. The BSO must order stop-work in the shared centrifuge room within 30 minutes. That halts both laboratories' runs and leaves the cell biology group asking when it can get back in. The BSO must also send the worker for medical evaluation within 60 minutes. The approved protocol says no post-exposure prophylaxis is needed, but the Occupational Health physician wants to see her. The clinic closes at 17:00, and after hours she would have to go to Marlow Falls Regional Medical Center. Her advisor and lab mates call asking whether they are at risk. A federal sponsor's program officer says informally that no NIH report is needed. Meanwhile the Iowa Corn Growers Board award requires notice within 72 hours, which is shorter than HSU's 7 days. The Director of Research Compliance has to reconcile the clock board with that award term. The IBC chair must classify the event and write down the basis for the decision. In a second laboratory, the freezer count does not match the inventory records. That lab is stuck until someone confirms it is a records discrepancy and not an incident, and no select agent report is filed. At 11:30 a student posts a "lab leak" claim on the campus forum, and the student newspaper calls for comment. Communications needs a fact sheet from the BSO and a holding statement that names no worker, laboratory or organism.

objectives.name: Worker Care and Containment
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to put the exposed graduate student's medical evaluation first by referring her to the Occupational Health Clinic within 60 minutes and before the 17:00 closing, with Marlow Falls Regional Medical Center as the after-hours fallback, while ordering and recording stop-work in the shared Lindgren third-floor centrifuge room within 30 minutes of the 09:20 call.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to classify the centrifuge tube failure in the IBC record, write down the basis for the classification, and separately confirm the second laboratory's freezer count mismatch as a records discrepancy without filing a select agent report, since HSU holds no select agents.

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to reconcile the EHS portal clock board with the Iowa Corn Growers Board award's 72-hour notice term, state which deadline governs where the stricter rule applies, and set the PI-to-BSO, IBC chair, sponsor and NIH notifications as who, how and when, without relying on the federal program officer's informal advice.

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to deliver the BSO's three-line fact sheet to University Communications within one hour and issue a holding statement and a single factual answer to the 11:30 campus-forum "lab leak" post and the student newspaper call, naming no worker, laboratory or organism and making no promise that nobody is at risk.

roles.name: Institutional Official / Vice President for Research
roles.description: Owns the institution's public posture, the decision with the IBC chair on whether anything about the organism is ever released, and the 72-hour telephone briefing to the Board of Regents' research committee chair.
standingOrders: Worker First: no reputational concern delays the student's medical evaluation or the stop-work order.
Stricter Clock: when the award term and HSU policy differ, follow the shorter deadline and say so in writing; informal sponsor advice changes nothing until it is in writing.
No Phantom Agents: HSU holds no select agents; any claim otherwise is checked by the BSO, and nobody reports it on a hunch.
One Voice: approve the holding statement but let University Communications speak; never promise that nobody is at risk.

roles.name: Biosafety Officer
roles.description: Manages incident classification, containment of the shared centrifuge room, medical referral of the exposed worker, the incident file and the fact sheet for Communications.
standingOrders: Stop Work: close the shared centrifuge room within 30 minutes and hold it closed until containment is verified, whatever the cell biology group's schedule.
Clinic Before Paperwork: send the worker for medical evaluation within 60 minutes even though the protocol says no prophylaxis is needed; watch the 17:00 clinic closing.
Search Before Conclusion: treat the freezer mismatch as a records question until transfers, destructions and labels have been checked.
Facts in an Hour: answer Communications' rumor check and send the three-line fact sheet within one hour: what happened, whether anyone was injured, whether the public is at risk.

roles.name: Institutional Biosafety Committee (IBC) chair
roles.description: Owns the classification of the event, the written basis for that classification, corrective actions, and what the committee reports to NIH and when.
standingOrders: Write the Basis: whatever the classification, record the facts and the rule it rests on before the record is closed.
Classify, Then Clock: the kind of event decides which NIH deadline applies; do not let the 30-day default stand if the facts point to an exposure that must be reported sooner.
Organism Stays Internal: release the organism's name publicly only on a joint decision with the IO for a public health need.

roles.name: Principal Investigator
roles.description: Owns the first report to the BSO, stop-work in the bacterial genetics laboratory, accounting for materials, support for the student, and the corrective actions on the centrifuge.
standingOrders: Report Early: a prompt good-faith report is never disciplined; give the BSO what you know and fill in the rest later.
Student Over Schedule: the student goes to the clinic before anyone finishes the run or the paperwork.
Answer Your People: tell lab mates and the advisor what is known about their risk, and send them to the BSO and Occupational Health rather than guessing.

roles.name: Director of Research Compliance
roles.team: Team E: Director of Research Compliance
roles.description: Manages the EHS portal clock board, notices to sponsors and regulators, and the reconciliation of the Iowa Corn Growers Board award's 72-hour term with HSU's 7-day sponsor clock.
standingOrders: Read the Award: the award term, not habit, sets the sponsor deadline; put the 72-hour clock on the board now.
Informal Is Not Official: a program officer's verbal 'no report needed' is logged but does not close any clock.
Who, How, When: record every notification with its recipient, method, time sent and the basis for its deadline.

roles.name: Director of University Communications
roles.description: Owns the holding statement, the one-time factual reply to the campus forum 'lab leak' post, the student newspaper inquiry and any use of HSUAlert.
standingOrders: Ready in Three: have a holding statement ready within 3 hours and post publicly only if interest continues past 24 hours.
Name Nobody: no worker, department, laboratory, organism or cause before the review, and nothing that tells a reader how to handle biological material.
Answer Once: reply to a wrong post once, with the facts, from the official account, after the BSO confirms them.
Hold the Alert: do not send HSUAlert for an event with no known public risk unless the BSO and IO agree that it is needed.

phases.title: The Cracked Tube
phases.goal: Tests whether the BSO and PI put the graduate student's medical evaluation first and record the first containment step in the 30- and 60-minute windows after the 09:20 call. Also tests whether the BSO gets the first facts to University Communications.
beats: (09:20) The PI's laboratory, Dr. Anika Rao's bacterial genetics group, calls the BSO. A tube cracked in a rotor in the shared Lindgren third-floor centrifuge room at 09:02. A graduate student may have had a face splash and a small cut to her gloved hand while working with a Risk Group 2 culture under an approved protocol. The 24-hour clock for the PI-to-BSO form starts. Incident number LI-2026-0142 is opened.

Stop-work deadline (09:50): the BSO must order and record stop-work for the shared centrifuge room. The room's door sign and a note at the Lindgren front desk are the visible record. Dr. Tomas Eklund's cell biology group is halted mid-run in the same room.

Referral deadline (10:20), under section 5 of the exposure plan: the BSO calls Dr. Mbeki at the Occupational Health Clinic. The approved protocol says no post-exposure prophylaxis is needed, but the physician still wants to see the student. The clinic closes at 17:00, and Marlow Falls Regional Medical Center is the after-hours fallback.

Unrelated item: a text from the Facilities operations center freezer monitoring system reports an ultralow freezer sensor offline on Lindgren's fourth floor. It goes to a laboratory manager and the BSO, and it is a battery fault, not related to the incident.

First technical note: the lab manager's photo of the centrifuge maintenance log shows that the rotor's vendor inspection is overdue. The sealed bucket lid on the failed position may not have held. This leaves open whether the failure stayed inside the rotor. The BSO's three-line fact sheet to Renata Delgado at University Communications (ext. 5-0200) is due by 10:20.

phases.title: Clocks and Crossed Signals
phases.goal: Tests whether the team can manage the work stoppage as it spreads to other groups and reconcile conflicting notification deadlines. It also tests whether players hold off on the select agent question until the facts support it.
beats: Time jump (10:30): the stoppage has spread. The cell biology group and two other third-floor users booked on the shared centrifuges cannot work. Dr. Tomas Eklund asks the BSO when they can get back in. The student's advisor and lab mates call asking whether they are at risk.

Red herring: a second laboratory reports that its freezer count does not match the EHS portal inventory. Someone in the room raises select agents and a possible Form 3 report. HSU holds no select agents, so the BSO must start a records search: transfer logs, unsigned destruction entries, box labels. This must happen before anyone draws a conclusion, and the team splits over it.

Visual for the room: a screenshot of the EHS portal clock board. It shows the sponsor notice set at 7 days, but the Iowa Corn Growers Board award (contact at cornboard.example) requires notice within 72 hours of discovery, which means by 09:02 on Friday, 16 October 2026. The Director of Research Compliance must reconcile the board and state that the stricter term governs.

A federal sponsor's program officer tells the Director of Research Compliance informally by phone that no NIH report is needed. The players must decide whether to record this or rely on it, given that the IBC classification has not yet been made.

Vendor estimate: the contract centrifuge vendor says a technician cannot inspect the rotor and chamber until Friday. A Campus Police query of the badge access log shows who entered the centrifuge room between 08:30 and 09:30, and the list is longer than expected.

phases.title: Reopen or Hold
phases.goal: Tests the single high-consequence decision about the shared room. In parallel, it tests the IBC classification and the public answer to a "lab leak" claim that names no worker, laboratory or organism.
beats: DECISION POINT (11:15): the BSO and IO, Dr. Ingrid Solheim, must choose between two options. Keeping the whole shared centrifuge room under stop-work until the vendor inspects it on Friday strands the cell biology group and delays sponsored runs. Reopening the room with the failed centrifuge tagged out and the room cleared by the BSO risks reopening a space whose cause is not yet confirmed. The decision and its basis must be written into LI-2026-0142.

IBC chair: under section 4 of the exposure plan, the chair must classify the centrifuge tube failure and write down the basis for the classification. That classification sets whether the NIH report is the 30-day report under the plan or an earlier one. The chair is notified the same day if the clinic's findings call for it.

Inject (11:30): a student posts a "lab leak in Lindgren" claim on the campus forum. The student newspaper then calls the department head and is redirected to ext. 5-0200. The reporter's deadline is 14:00. Under section 3 of the Communications plan, the statement must name no worker, laboratory or organism and must not promise that nobody is at risk. The IO approves any mention of a worker's health.

Tension with partners and colleagues: Dr. Tomas Eklund pushes back on whatever the room decision is. The second laboratory is still stuck until the freezer mismatch is confirmed as a records discrepancy. The question of using HSUAlert comes up, and only University Communications or Campus Police can send it.

Worker support (12:00): the clinic reports that the student has been seen. Only fitness for duty is released to the BSO. Under section 6 of the exposure plan, the PI offers her alternate duties, and Dean Dr. Ruth Halloran's same-day note to building staff names the Employee Assistance Program at ext. 5-0250.

phases.title: Back in the Room
phases.goal: Tests a phased, verified return to work and correction of the public record. It also tests that every notification is set as who, how and when against the deadline that governs it.
beats: Restoration claim (12:20): the BSO clears the room in this order. First the room, then the biosafety cabinet and the remaining centrifuges, then each laboratory's bookings. The failed centrifuge stays tagged out, and the clearance is recorded on paper at the Lindgren front desk and in the EHS portal.

Hurdle: the vendor's replacement rotor is the wrong model for the unit, and the correct part is days away. A second centrifuge then throws an imbalance fault on its first run, so players must decide whether to stop again or allow the run to continue.

Verification: the second laboratory's records search finds the cause of the freezer mismatch. A transfer was logged on paper but not in the EHS portal inventory. The BSO records it as a records discrepancy, and no select agent report or Form 3 is filed.

Media follow-up (13:30): the student newspaper publishes a story that names the building and calls it a "leak." University Communications must decide whether to request a correction. A single factual answer goes back to the forum thread.

Notifications are set as who, how and when: the Director of Research Compliance sends notice to the Iowa Corn Growers Board before 09:02 on 16 October, which is the stricter rule. The BSO notifies the IBC chair. NIH is notified according to the IBC classification and not the program officer's informal advice. Risk Management is notified only if there is a medical claim. The BSO's after-action note opens the corrective action for the rotor inspection schedule. ENDEX at 13:15.

hotwash.methodDescription: Ask the room for three things that went well and three that broke or failed during the response. Go around the room one team at a time (BSO and EHS, the laboratories, Research Compliance, Communications, Campus Police and leadership) and write every answer on the whiteboard in two columns before you discuss any of them.

questions.text: At 09:30 (I-02), the cell biology group at the centrifuge room door asked to walk in for their tubes. They also told you that two people who were in the room when the tube cracked had heard nothing from anyone. Then at 10:55 (I-09b), the badge log showed eight entries and a visitor badge, while your list had three people. When did you stop trusting your list of who was exposed? Did Lena Park reach the Occupational Health Clinic within 60 minutes, with Marlow Falls Regional Medical Center as the after-hours fallback? Who followed up with the other people on the badge log, and when?

The 09:55 email (I-04) showed a rotor inspection two months overdue, a lid seated crooked and a film on the inside of the chamber window. Did you treat those facts as evidence for classifying the event in the IBC record, or as a maintenance ticket for Facilities? When Raj called at 11:50 (I-15) and accounted for the 14 vials as a paper transfer that never reached the portal, who confirmed in writing that it was a records discrepancy with no select agent report, given that HSU holds no select agents? Where did you write down the basis for each decision?

The EHS portal clock board (I-08) showed the sponsor notice due in 7 days. The Award Terms tab in the same portal required notice to the Iowa Corn Growers Board within 72 hours of discovery at 09:02. When did someone notice that the board had never picked up that term? Who decided that the stricter deadline governs, and was that written down? Did the PI-to-BSO, IBC chair, sponsor and NIH notifications each get a named owner, a method and a time, or did the program officer's informal advice fill the gap?

At 11:20 (I-12), the department head wanted a written choice between keeping the room closed until Friday (A) and reopening it that afternoon (B). Dr. Tomas Eklund cited a sponsor deadline, while the vendor had said not to run either machine and nobody yet knew why the tube cracked. Did the operations side understand what the technical team was telling them about the film and the uninspected rotor, and the other way round? Who signed the decision? Was the stop-work order from 09:20 recorded clearly enough to hold up under that pressure?

The 'lab leak' post appeared at 11:30 (I-13). The Herald's 14:00 deadline followed, then the sergeant's offer of an HSUAlert at 11:53 (I-15). By 12:45 (I-21), the Herald article said 'the university did not respond.' What did HSU actually say publicly before you had confirmed facts, and when? Did the BSO's three-line fact sheet reach University Communications within the hour? What made you decide whether to send the HSUAlert? Did your holding statement avoid naming the worker, the laboratory or the organism, and avoid promising that nobody is at risk?

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment. Players are evaluated on how the HSU research and biosafety team works together, not as individuals, and a prompt good-faith report is treated as the start of a conversation, not a finding.
The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented. Players accept the inject facts, including clinic hours, vendor dates and the clock board entries, as they appear in the room.

Players respond in accordance with existing HSU plans, policies and procedures, including the biosafety roles, the notification clocks and University Communications guidance. Where no plan addresses an issue, players say what they would decide, who decides it and how it is recorded.
Players have only the information shown in each module and its injects. They do not know the cause of the tube failure or how any discrepancy turns out until an inject tells them.
Halvorsen State University holds no select agents. Any select agent question has to be settled on the facts available in the room.
artificialities: Time is compressed. Each 60-minute module stands for one hour of a single Tuesday morning, and Time Jump cards move the clock forward between modules.

A SimCell plays everyone outside the room. This includes the Occupational Health Clinic, Prairieline Lab Services, the Iowa Corn Growers Board program contact, the federal program officer, the insurer, Campus Police, The Halvorsen Herald, social media and forum users, department heads and laboratory staff.

The EHS portal and its clock board, badge access records, freezer monitoring, HSUAlert and the official social media accounts are named as they appear in the plans but are not touched. Players describe the entries, alerts and posts they would make.
Injects such as calls, emails, posts, screenshots and articles are delivered on paper or on screen. Nothing is actually sent to a regulator, sponsor, reporter or the public.

**Module 2: Clocks and Crossed Signals (10:15–11:15)**

It is 10:15. At 09:20 the bacterial genetics lab manager reported that at 09:02 a tube cracked in a rotor in the shared third-floor centrifuge room. A graduate student reported a possible splash to her face and a nick through her glove while working with the lab's Risk Group 2 culture under the approved protocol. She used the eyewash and washed her hand. The rotor is still in the centrifuge with the lid closed. Two cell biology staff were in the room with her. The Occupational Health physician insisted on seeing her in person today, offered a 10:15 slot and asked for the agent information sheet. The physician also noted that the clinic closes at 17:00 and that Marlow Falls Regional Medical Center is the after-hours option. The student had asked to come after lunch.

A stop-work sign is on the room door. The maintenance log shows the last rotor inspection on 14 Aug 2025, about two months overdue. There is a film on the inside of the chamber window. The centrifuge was bought on the Iowa Corn Growers Board award. A fourth-floor freezer sensor (ULT-L4-17) went offline at 09:21, and its lab manager has asked whether it is connected. At 10:05 a student post about the taped-off door began spreading, with one reply asking about 'select agent stuff'. The Halvorsen Herald wants answers by 11:30.

The stoppage has now spread. Two other groups have been turned away from the room, and Dr. Tomas Eklund wants a time for getting back in. The student's advisor and lab mates are calling to ask whether they are at risk. No written update has gone to the floor.
keyIssues: Managing a stoppage that is spreading, and putting out one written update to the floor without saying more than is known.
The clock board's 7-day sponsor default against the award's own notice term.
Pressure to report a select agent loss before the facts support it, at a university that holds no select agents.
Making sure everyone who was in the room has been identified and referred, not only the people on the first list.

**Module 3: Reopen or Hold (11:15–12:15)**

It is 11:15. The shared third-floor centrifuge room has been under stop-work for nearly two hours. The cell biology run finished at 10:10, and its tubes are still in the second centrifuge. Three more groups have cancelled afternoon bookings. Prairieline Lab Services cannot inspect before Friday 16 Oct at 08:00. Until then it asks that the rotor, buckets and lid stay in place and that neither centrifuge in the room is run. A loaner unit can be delivered Thursday.

The graduate student, Lena, was seen at the clinic at 10:20. She has a baseline taken, nothing is indicated today, and she has a follow-up on Thursday at 09:00. She is not to enter the room before then. The physician recorded the event as a possible mucous membrane splash to the face and a percutaneous injury through the glove, and is still waiting for the PI's written description. Badge records show eight entries to the suite between 08:30 and 09:30, three of them with no exit recorded. One cell biology technician has not come in to the clinic.

On the fourth floor, a quarterly count found 14 vials missing from rack C of ULT-L4-09, and the reason is not yet known. The clock board still shows 7 days for the sponsor row, and the IBC chair has not classified LI-2026-0142. The student post has passed 300 reposts, a 'missing vials' rumor is running alongside it, and the Herald's 11:30 deadline is 15 minutes away.
keyIssues: Whether to keep the whole room closed until Friday or reopen it in part when the vendor's advice and the cause are both unresolved, and who signs the decision.
The IBC classification and its written basis, against informal advice that 'it doesn't need an NIH report'.
Answering a 'lab leak' post and a reporter who wants the lab named, without naming the worker, the lab or the organism and without promising that nobody is at risk.
Whether to send an HSUAlert in answer to parents' calls.
Keeping the clinic's findings private from the advisor, the insurer and the Dean's staff note.

**Module 4: Back in the Room (12:15–13:15)**

It is 12:15. The department head has a signed written answer on the third-floor centrifuge room, and the BSO's phased reopening is under way. The failed centrifuge is tagged out, untouched and still under its sealed lid. Four groups want back in at once, and the cell biology postdoc is waiting at the door with an empty ice bucket. Lena is fit for duty with a restriction: no entry to the room before her 15 Oct follow-up. The second cell biology technician has been re-referred but has not shown up.

The 14 vials from the fourth floor were found in ULT-L4-12, moved on 21 August under a paper log that was never entered in the EHS portal. The portal still shows 212 in rack C, and nobody has signed a closure. The clock board now has a 72-hour sponsor row due 16 Oct 09:02 that nobody has acted on. The BSO's first written report to the IBC chair is still a draft.

The forum thread has passed 400 upvotes. The Herald has moved its deadline to 14:00, but its editor says a web story will go up 'when it's ready'. The Dean's note to Lindgren staff is due by 15:00.
